commit.message:
0.36.1: a selector's Http404 fails the tool call as not found (#127)

* Answer a selector's Http404 as not found by raising the kernel floor

A selector written with get_object_or_404 raises Http404, which dispatch let
through and which aborted the agent run. django-service-specs 0.10.0 answers it
as a missing row, so the call now fails with ToolFailed("not found") like a
DoesNotExist, and a read with allow_none returns None. No code here changes:
the floor is the fix, and the not-found tests are parametrised over the three
ways a selector reports a missing row, for a read, a write's instance selector
and a full agent run. An exception_map entry for Http404 is no longer reached
for a selector, which a test now holds.

The floor moves with djangorestframework-mcp-server's: the two routes reach one
spec, so with only one raised the same selector is a not-found on one route and
an error on the other. See drf-mcp#188.

commit.message:
Release 0.36.0: server-supplied arguments on drf-services 0.58 (#124)

* Adapt to djangorestframework-services 0.58.0 and refuse PASSTHROUGH at construction

Floor djangorestframework-services at 0.58.0 (dropping the ceiling) and
declare django-service-specs, importing the kernel-owned names from it.

SpecToolset and SpecCapability accept only UnknownArguments.REJECT and
IGNORE: PASSTHROUGH, which drf-services refuses on every call, now raises
ImproperlyConfigured when the toolset is built.

Tests and docs move from SpecRegistry.register(agent_contract=) to the
spec's own reads= and field_audiences=, and assert 0.58.0's answers where
the toolset surfaces them: the missing-field wording, a selector-less
SelectorSpec refused at construction, REJECT over a filter_set, and a
bare mapping that does not advertise a spec's reads but routes them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name the tool in build-time refusals and refuse native specs with TypeError

drf-services' refusals raised while the toolset is built are re-raised
prefixed with the tool: every spec is compiled first, and each tool's
output projection is wrapped the same way, so a selector-less spec, a
read clashing with a list argument, a field_audiences key naming no
output field and two label fields all say which tool they are about.

A django-service-specs spec reaching SpecToolset or SpecCapability, from
a registry or a mapping, is refused with a TypeError naming the tool and
the drf-services constructors, where it died on an AttributeError.

The registry page and the changelog state plainly that a QueryParam read
naming a selector parameter is refused from the registry and routed from
registry.specs(), and that the seam release fixes the asymmetry. The
filter_set and **kwargs REJECT change is marked breaking, the
unknown_arguments refusal is tested for "drop", the list-name read test
goes through SpecToolset, and a broken docs anchor is fixed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* State the 0.35.x behaviour truthfully and mark the breaking changes

PASSTHROUGH up to 0.35.x served a call and forwarded its undeclared keys,
into a service's data among others; the changelog, the refusal's docstring
and its test now say that drf-services 0.58 retired it, rather than that a
mount used to abort on its first call.

The register(agent_contract=...) removal, the selector=None refusal and
the refusal of a field_audiences key naming no output field are marked
breaking, each with what to do instead. The registry/mapping difference
for a read shadowing a selector parameter is described as a difference a
later release makes consistent, and a test pins the mapping route.

The TypeError for a value that is not a drf-services ServiceSpec or
SelectorSpec now says exactly that, points only a kernel spec at
django_service_specs.dispatch and a PolymorphicServiceSpec at its
variants, and the projection's unreachable name= argument is gone.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add tool_server_arguments, deprecate mount-level channels, serve a spec's own input reads

SpecToolset and SpecCapability take tool_server_arguments, a ServerArguments
per tool: bound values the call always carries and withheld names it never
takes, checked at construction with the kernel's check_server_arguments and
applied first in each call, before the required-arguments check and before
the channels are split. Both leave the advertised schema and the
instructions; a caller's value for one is dropped and logged by name.

query_params, tool_query_params, url_kwargs and tool_url_kwargs warn with
DeprecationWarning naming the spec's reads and tool_server_arguments.

A spec's own QueryParam read naming an input the tool advertises is no
longer a toolset channel on the registry route, so it builds and serves as
it does from registry.specs(); a mount declaring the same name is still
refused as a shadow.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep a bound selection out of the render retry, and cover filter_set reads

A render rejecting a bound QueryParam value is a configuration bug, so it is
raised rather than answered with a retry naming an argument the model was
never offered. A spec's own read of a filter_set field is served alike from
both routes, and the deprecation's frame walk stops at the outermost frame.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bind only a tool the run's scope reaches, and teach reads in the quickstart

The registry page's per-run scope recipe withheld every scope name a run did
not bind, so a tool reading only another scope name lost its argument and a
required one made the build fail. It now binds a tool only when the run binds
one of its scope reads, withholds only the optional siblings, and the tests
run the page's block as written.

The quickstart's read-shaping and route-capture examples declare reads on the
spec and bind scope with tool_server_arguments instead of the deprecated
toolset knobs. The deprecation warning names the class it was passed to, the
dropped-argument log is worded for withheld names too, and the frame walk, the
bindings copy and the url_kwargs the shadow check reads each have a test that
fails without them. The changelog states the migration for bare **kwargs
selectors and the UrlKwarg pairing the registry now builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Bump version to 0.36.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Release 0.35.0 (#115)

* Raise the djangorestframework-services floor to 0.56.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Adopt drf-services 0.56.0's readers and close #104 to #108

Read a kwargs provider's keys through drf-services' provider_keys, the
reader dispatch checks the call with, in place of the toolset's own
annotation reader. That reader counted a key as declinable wherever
UnsetType appeared inside its type (#104), made the whole provider
untyped when one annotation named a TYPE_CHECKING-only type (#105), and
read a generic TypedDict's key as the bare type variable (#106).

Refuse at construction a list selector parameter named page or limit,
and any spec input a QueryParam also names, since the toolset strips
each before the selector runs (#107).

Take a return schema's allow_none from can_present_nothing, so a
service whose re-read can find no row, or one declaring allow_none with
nothing to re-read, admits the None it returns (#108).

Leave a key any callable in a service call marks NotClientInput out of
what the target lookup contributes, as server_owned_keys names them,
unless the input serializer declares it, and read the input schema
under the argument binding dispatch is called with.

Update the tests 0.56.0 changes: a many or both-lookups spec is now
refused by ServiceSpec, a declined parameter the model left out is a
missing-argument retry, and an unresolvable provider annotation no
longer hides every key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* State the drf-services 0.56 floor in the compatibility table and the pin comment

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Check a QueryParam against the names a tool offers the model

The construction check that refuses a QueryParam sharing an input's name
read the spec's own reflection, which was wrong in both directions. It
missed a service's target lookup parameters, which the tool advertises
as the call's input, so a required lookup parameter was answered as a
missing argument of every call carrying it and a defaulted one resolved
on its default. And it refused a selector parameter a typed kwargs=
provider fills, the ordinary way to route a query parameter to a
selector, where nothing is lost.

The check now reads _caller_schema, the reader the tool's schema is built
from: the selector's or the target lookup's parameters less what a
provider declares it fills and what the server keeps, keeping what a
provider may decline, plus a service's input serializer fields. The
refusal says whether the selector, the service or its target lookup
takes the name.

Docs and changelog: the quickstart and the #108 entry say an undeclared
None is still handed to the model against an object schema, with
allow_none=True as the declaration that admits it; a Changed entry
covers a LIST output with no selector refusing a return that is not a
set of rows, and its test now asserts what dispatch returns; the
NotClientInput entry no longer claims a filter_set field is protected.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name the typed-provider route in the QueryParam refusal

A kwargs= provider whose TypedDict declares the parameter is now exempt
from the refusal, and it is the usual way to hand a query parameter to a
selector, so the message and the quickstart offer it as the first remedy.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Release 0.35.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Release 0.34.0: reword model-facing lines one at a time with AgentConventions (#114)

* Make the model-facing wording overridable one line at a time

AgentConventions is a frozen dataclass with one field per sentence the
toolset writes for the model: the lines of the instructions block, the
heading of the unavailable-operations list, a handle field's fallback
description, the scope sentence on a paged tool's QueryParam and render
retry, and the missing-argument retry. Every default is the previous
text byte for byte, pinned by tests that read it through the public
surface and pass against the previous release unchanged.

SpecToolset and SpecCapability take conventions=, defaulting to None
(AgentConventions()). A field changes what a line says and never whether
it appears: the toolset still gates each line on a tool that can act on
it, per step. None drops a line. Placeholders are checked when the
instance is built and a template that cannot be rendered raises
ImproperlyConfigured naming the field. instructions= beside a change to
a block line is refused, since the override would ignore it; the four
fields that land outside the block apply either way.

SpecCapability.from_toolset keeps a toolset's conventions because it
wraps that instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Release 0.34.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Scope the conventions claims and refuse a blank missing-argument retry

The docs said every sentence the toolset writes for the model is a field of
AgentConventions. The fields cover the instructions block and its unavailable
heading, a handle's fallback description, the read-shaping scope sentence and
the missing-argument retry; argument descriptions such as limit's and page's,
and the other retries, stay fixed. README, quickstart, CHANGELOG and the class
docstring now say exactly that.

missing_arguments="" (or whitespace) is now refused with ImproperlyConfigured
naming the field, for the same reason None is: the model would get an empty
retry. Elsewhere "" is accepted and leaves a blank line, which the quickstart
now warns about and a test pins.

The doubled-brace test now sets every field that takes no placeholder, so a
site passing one through unrendered fails it. Three sentences claiming the
unavailable list is always appended after an instructions= override are
qualified for unavailable_heading=None, with a test, and a real Agent is shown
to take get_instructions returning None as no instructions, attached as a
toolset or through either capability route.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Release 0.32.0: a read-shaping value the serializer rejects while rendering is a retry, not a dead run (#96)

* Retry a read-shaping value the output serializer rejects while rendering

A read-shaping param is the one argument used while the result renders
rather than while the call dispatches, so a selection strict django-restql
rejects escaped the run as a raw DRF ValidationError. The render call is now
wrapped: the consumer's exception map first, then a ModelRetry naming the
argument, but only when the caller supplied a non-null value for a declared
QueryParam. A seeded default, an explicit null or no value at all keeps the
error loud, and only validation errors are converted.

A list tool's QueryParam description, the derived read-shaping instruction
and the retry now say that on a page the param applies to each item in
`items`, never to the envelope.

Validation retries now carry one `path: message` line per error instead of
the repr of DRF's ErrorDetail objects, on the dispatch path as well.

django-restql joins the dev group for an end-to-end test against the real
serializer, with pypeg2's compile-time escape warnings filtered.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Treat an explicit null read-shaping argument as omitted

QueryParam documents `{"fields": null}` as a model declining to fill the
param, with any declared default still applying. The toolset forwarded the
null instead, and the off-HTTP request stringifies every value, so the
serializer read the four characters `None`: strict django-restql cannot parse
that and ended the run over an argument the model had not sent. The key is
still popped either way, so unknown-argument handling never sees it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Changelog for the render-time read-shaping retry

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Release 0.32.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Name several rejected read-shaping params with "or", as the MCP transport does

"`query` and `fields` were rejected" claims both were, when the serializer
does not say which one it refused.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Describe read-shaping errors without assuming one selection library

The toolset never reads a QueryParam's value, so nothing in the render
retry is specific to django-restql; several comments, the quickstart and
the changelog read as if it were. They now lead with any serializer
refusing a selection and keep django-restql as one example. A new test
runs a fields selection the serializer parses itself, refusing in its own
words, and pins that the retry names the param and quotes the serializer
verbatim.

commit.message:
Release 0.31.0: leave an operation whose condition is unmet out of a step's tools (#94)

* Leave an operation whose condition is unmet out of a step's tools

An Affordance on a ServiceSpec whose `when` is a callable reads only the
pool's seeds, so while it is unmet every call of that tool is refused
whatever the model sends. get_tools now asks those conditions on each step,
through drf-services' unmet_operation_affordance, and omits a tool while one
is unmet. The step's instructions are derived from the tools it offers and
end by naming each missing operation with its reason, so the model can tell
the user why instead of guessing.

Conditions run in the dispatch thread under the toolset's thread_sensitive
and executor, against a pool built through build_context, and close any
connection they open, as a dispatch does. A toolset declaring no such
condition asks nothing and takes no hop. Call-time enforcement is unchanged.

Floors djangorestframework-services at 0.54.0, where both helpers first
exist.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Release 0.31.0

commit.message:
Take a many=True spec's list as one named tool argument (#91)

* Take a many=True spec's list as one named tool argument

A ServiceSpec declaring many=True was refused when the toolset was built,
because it validates a JSON array and a model's tool arguments are always an
object. drf-services now reads such a list out of the argument
ServiceSpec.many_argument names, so the toolset dispatches every call with
many_as_argument=True and the refusal is gone.

The parameter schema is drf-services' wrapper object, with declared query
params and URL kwargs merged beside the list. A QueryParam or UrlKwarg named
after the list argument is refused with ImproperlyConfigured, since it would be
popped before dispatch and take the list with it. The return schema of a
many=True tool describes an array, where reading the RETRIEVE output selector's
kind alone advertised an object. Item errors reach the model as a ModelRetry
keyed under the argument and the item's index.

* Floor djangorestframework-services at 0.53.0

Every service dispatch passes many_as_argument=True, which 0.53.0 adds, so
below it every call raises TypeError while the package still imports.

commit.message:
Name a refusal's rule, return None where a tool finds nothing, refuse many=True specs (release 0.29.0) (#88)

* Name the rule a refused call failed on, not only the reason

drf-services raises ActionUnavailable(reason, code=...) when an Affordance
condition refuses a call. Every ServiceError became ToolFailed(str(exc)), so the
model read only the reason and the code survived on __cause__ alone. ToolFailed
carries a message and nothing else, and a transport forwards that message as the
tool result, so the refusal now reads "<reason> (code: <code>)". Every other
ServiceError keeps its message, the consumer's map still runs first, and the
conventions block tells the model the code is the one an affordances answer
carries.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Release 0.29.0

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Refuse many=True service specs, and return None where a tool finds nothing

A ServiceSpec with many=True validates its input as a JSON array, and a
model's tool arguments are always an object, so the tool was offered and
answered every call with a retry no model could satisfy. The toolset now
refuses it at construction with ImproperlyConfigured, as the MCP
transport does, naming the named-list-field shape that works.

A nullable retrieve that found no row, and a service that returned None,
reached the model as the output serializer's blank row. drf-services
0.52.1 renders a single None as None; the tests pin that both return it.

Advertise the affordances object a tool's payload carries (release 0.28.0) (#87)

* Advertise the affordances object a tool's payload carries

drf-services 0.51 added SelectorSpec.affordances, and render_for_audience
adds an affordances object to every item a spec declaring them renders.
The return schema this toolset builds itself never passed the declaration
to output_to_json_schema, so the model was handed items carrying a key the

affordances are the conditions it is checked against and are never
rendered, so they are not advertised. A spec declaring none keeps a
byte-identical schema.

The drf-services floor rises to >=0.51, where the argument and the
attribute first exist; both are used while building every tool definition,
so the floor is hard. The compatibility table in CLAUDE.md, which still
read 0.48, now agrees with the pin.

commit.message:
Stop a test committing rows nothing rolls back (#83)

test_call_tool_uses_the_projection_built_at_construction was marked django_db
without transaction=True and creates two rows through acreate. In an async test
there is no synchronous frame above the loop, so sync_to_async routes to
asgiref's shared thread -- a different connection, in autocommit -- while
pytest-django's rollback wraps this thread's connection and nothing else. Both
rows committed.

One correction to how this was described to me: the rows do not survive to the
end of the session. They survive until the next transaction=True test, whose
teardown truncates every table, sixteen tests later. That is not a footnote, it
decided the shape of the guard below -- a session-scoped "the database is empty
at the end" assertion would have passed on this defect while sixteen tests ran
against a polluted database.

Creating the rows on the test's own thread is the cheaper-looking fix and does
not work: the dispatch under test runs on the shared thread, and rows still
uncommitted in this thread's transaction are invisible from there, so the
assertion would read back an empty page. Measured, not assumed. transaction=True
it is, which is what the file's two other dispatch-writing tests already do. The
cost was measured too and is below the noise floor here, which the comment says
will not be true on a bigger schema.

tests/conftest.py now reads the committed contents of the database after every
test, over a read-only sqlite3 handle of its own -- not the ORM, because this
suite asserts on Django connection state and a check that opened one would
perturb what it measures. It accepts two states, unchanged or back to pristine,
so a truncating test is not blamed for cleaning up, and it moves its expectation
before raising so the accusation lands on one test rather than on the sixteen
that merely ran afterwards. Its first version reproduced exactly that confusion.

commit.message:
A failed tool call says it failed (#79)

Four failures were returned as ordinary values -- a business-rule
refusal, an unresolved target, a dispatch past its deadline, and a
result over the byte ceiling all came back as {"error": ...}. pydantic-ai
marks a returned value outcome='success' by default, so every one of
them travelled as a successful call carrying prose, and a client
rendering tool results had nothing to read but the words inside.

All four now raise ToolFailed, which is the signal upstream provides for
exactly this: a call that is done and has failed, reported to the model
without the retry instructions ModelRetry prepends and without consuming
the retry budget. The wording the model sees is unchanged at all four
sites; what changes is that the return is marked failed.

The two obvious sites are the domain refusal and the missing row --
"a missing resource" is the first case ToolFailed's own docstring names.
The other two were judged rather than swept along. Both had a docstring
arguing for a dict "rather than an exception, because killing the run
denies the model the chance to answer" -- and that argument is about an
ordinary exception. ToolFailed kills nothing and burns no budget, so the
stated reason survives intact and needed rewording rather than
reversing, while a timed-out dispatch rendering as a completed call is
precisely the defect being fixed.

The byte ceiling carries a compatibility cost, called out in the
changelog: an enforce_result_bytes override that delegates to super()
and inspects the return now gets an exception instead.

The floor moves to pydantic-ai-slim>=2.16, bisected against the wheels
rather than inferred -- ToolFailed is absent at 2.15.0 and present at
2.16.0 -- and the whole suite was run against a venv pinned there. A
sibling already declares the same floor for the same symbol.

The instructions no longer tell the model to look for {"error": ...}, a
key this toolset had stopped sending, and seven other prose sites that
described the returned shape are corrected with it. The exception_map
seam is unchanged and now has a test proving it: a consumer handler that
returns a value still produces a successful call, which is the escape
hatch for a failure a project would rather express as an answer.

commit.message:
Widen output_extras unconditionally and take the break (#75)

``output_extras`` gained a keyword-only ``dispatch_result`` carrier, and the
call was widened only where a signature accepted it: ``_declares_dispatch_result``
read the class's method at construction, ``SpecToolset._extras_for`` dropped the
keyword for an override that predated it. All of that is removed; the carrier is
passed on every call, and an override carrying the 0.23.0 signature now raises
``TypeError`` naming the argument.

The compatibility it bought is worth close to nothing. ``output_extras`` became
a seam in 0.23.0, published one day earlier -- the population of subclasses
overriding a one-day-old method on a 0.x package is as close to empty as a
population gets. The cost is permanent: signature introspection in a package
that had none of it, kept long past the transition it was for, since nothing
announces the day it stopped being needed.

It was also not compatible so much as quiet. The answer resolved in ``__init__``
off the *class*, so an ``output_extras`` assigned onto an instance afterwards
was never seen: the override kept being called without the carrier it declared,
nothing raised, nothing logged, and the first sign of it a wrong answer
downstream from an extras pool missing what the override was written to add. A
gate that silently does not run is the worst outcome available here, and the
shim manufactured one while appearing to prevent one.

The default pool is unchanged -- a key the HTTP path does not supply would still
reach an output-context provider that never declared it -- and applying
``response_finalizer`` or resolving a callable ``success_status`` stays declined.

The suite carried an instance of the break itself: the 0.23.0 test asserting an
override reaches the resolved-data pool was written against the old signature
and now declares the parameter. The new test pins the break as loud, and fails
against the previous tree with "DID NOT RAISE".

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Give output_extras the DispatchResult, and correlate the last two log lines (#74)

``output_extras``' own docstring named ``DispatchResult.service_result`` as the
thing the default pool withholds and closed by offering an override as the
escape hatch. The escape hatch did not work: ``_call_spec`` read ``kind``,
``value`` and ``kind`` again off the dispatch result and let the carrier go, so
no seam could reach the flags an upsert's ``created`` rides on -- nor
``instance`` (the pre-mutation target) or ``data`` (the validated input), which
were dropped on the same floor. The loss is conditional, which is why it
survived: with no ``output_selector_spec`` the service's return *is* ``value``.
It is exactly the upsert that re-fetches which cannot answer created-vs-updated.

The carrier is passed only to an override that declares it. ``output_extras`` is
public and shipped without the parameter, so the class's signature is read once
at construction and the call widened only where it fits; a subclass carrying the
old signature is called the way it was written rather than raising ``TypeError``
on the next tool call. Applying ``response_finalizer`` or resolving a callable
``success_status`` stays declined -- both are status-code machinery a toolset
has no wire for.

The dispatch-timeout and result-bound warnings now carry the run's correlation
fields too. Both were said to be module-level helpers with no ``RunContext``;
``_with_deadline`` has one call site inside ``call_tool``, and the bound is
reached through ``enforce_result_bytes``, which already receives ``ctx``. These
are the two lines that fire when a run misbehaves, which is when an uncorrelated
line is worth least.

Finally, the derived instructions block is memoised. It is a pure function of
four attributes the constructor assigns and nothing reassigns, and pydantic-ai
asks for instructions on every model step. Tidiness rather than throughput: the
cost is tens of microseconds per spec against round trips measured in seconds.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Remove the deprecated ordering_fields knob (#68)

`SpecToolset(ordering_fields=…)` / `tool_ordering_fields=` and their
`SpecCapability` counterparts are gone, along with the machinery that
existed only to serve them: the two-vocabulary construction refusal, the
`ordering` enum written into a list tool's input schema, the enum
validation at dispatch, `_PageArgs.ordering`, and the `queryset.order_by`
in `_shape_list`. Passing either keyword now raises `TypeError` rather
than being silently ignored.

Deprecated in 0.16.0 (2026-08-11), four minors ago. A Django model
carries its own `Meta.ordering`, the HTTP path already declares ordering
through a `filter_set`, and django-filter's `OrderingFilter` does more
than a list of raw ORM paths can — so one vocabulary now serves HTTP and
every agent transport alike.

The `filter_set` path is untouched: an `OrderingFilter` is still found
under whatever name it was declared, its labelled choices still reach the
model through the reflected schema, and its value is still routed through
`filter_data` so it reaches the FilterSet and not the selector's kwargs.
`_pop_filter_ordering` and `_spec_ordering_argument` stay exactly as they
were.

The `FieldError` arm around `_shape_list` went with the knob, because it
only ever caught the sort the toolset applied itself. It never covered a
`filter_set`-declared sort and its removal does not change that path:
Django validates a plain-string `order_by` eagerly, so a `param_map`
target that is not a column raises inside `dispatch_spec`, above where
the arm sat. The failure table in the quickstart claimed otherwise and is
corrected; a test now pins the real behaviour.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Adopt drf-services 0.48: paginate list results, publish a return schema (#66)

Four changes that land together because 0.48 is what makes them possible.

**Every list-selector result is now a page.** `page` and `limit` were merged
into every list tool's parameter schema from the beginning while the payload
was a bare slice with no total and no clamp -- so a model asking for a
collection received 50 of 51 rows with nothing telling it more existed. Results
now carry drf-services' published envelope (`items` / `page` / `totalPages` /
`hasNext`), sliced by the shared `paginate_output` shaper, so the two agent
transports count and clamp through one implementation. An omitted `limit` is
now a bounded page rather than "everything", and it says so. The untyped-value
coercion stays here: a malformed `limit` is still a `ModelRetry`, which is the
one place a public endpoint and an in-process toolset legitimately differ.

**`ToolDefinition.return_schema` is populated**, from the same spec and the same
projection as the payload, so a hidden field is absent from both and the schema
and the result finally agree about the envelope. `include_return_schema` stays
at pydantic-ai's default; the opt-in is already pydantic-ai's own. This
corrects a claim the changelog made twice and `docs/agent-audience.md` opened
on -- a `ToolDefinition` has carried `return_schema` throughout.

**`json_schema_registry=`** threads a `JsonSchemaRegistry` into every schema
generated here, including the reflected read behind the ordering predicate, so
a project's own field or filter type no longer reaches the model as "any value".

**The renamed audience symbols** are adopted (`FieldMarking`, `MARKING`,
`AudienceProjection`, `OfflineContract`, `audience_projection_for_spec`,
`render_for_audience`), and a labelled `ChoiceFilter` -- so a FilterSet-derived
`ordering` -- now travels as `oneOf` const options rather than a bare `enum`.

Floor raised to `djangorestframework-services>=0.48` as the final step.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Find the sort argument under whatever name it was declared (#64)

The only two runtime DeprecationWarnings in the family are both ordering_fields,
and both send consumers to a django-filter OrderingFilter. Nothing requires that
filter to be named `ordering`, and the predicate tested for the literal string.

A project whose filter is called `sorting` followed the migration correctly and
lost two things. The usage instruction was dropped, so the tool advertised a
large enum with no guidance. And the value was never popped out of the callable's
kwarg pool, so a selector declaring **kwargs received a read-shaping argument it
never asked for -- the exact hazard _pop_filter_ordering's own docstring
describes for the `ordering` case, arriving through the door it was watching.

The sort itself always worked: filter_data stayed defaulted to params and the
FilterSet reads params either way. That is why nobody found it, and the
regression test that passes against both implementations says so.

The name is now asked for rather than assumed, by finding the filter that defines
get_ordering_value -- the method OrderingFilter declares and nothing else in the
hierarchy does. Duck-typed, so django-filter stays an optional extra this package
never imports, and a project's own subclass is found too. Falls back to the
literal `ordering` for the two cases a filter_set cannot answer: a selector whose

commit.message:
Release 0.19.0 — toolset request-context integrity, and a floor that closes the shared-request race (#61)

* Authorize a toolset call the way the same spec is authorized elsewhere

A spec exposed as an agent tool was gated differently from the same spec
exposed over MCP, in two ways that a permission class cannot see.

`view.action` was never set, so every spec authorized against `None`. A
permission class shaped `if view.action in {...}: strict else: allow` took
the permissive arm on every agent call. It is now the tool name -- the
identity the model called, and what the MCP transport reports for the same
spec. `build_context` takes and forwards `action`, so an override can
rewrite it for a class that branches on viewset action names.

A configured `http_request`'s query string reached the spec whenever a tool
declared no query params: the empty declaration was passed as `None`, and
`build_offline_context` replaces the wrapped request's `GET` only for a
mapping. A field-selection serializer or a `filter_set` could then reshape a
result through a channel neither the tool schema nor the model chose. Every
call now passes a mapping, empty declaration included.

Raise the drf-services floor to 0.44, which stops `build_offline_context`
writing to the request it is given. Below it, one configured request is
shared across every call a toolset makes, so two concurrent runs overwrite
each other's query params with no error, and the caller's own `method` /
`GET` / `user` stay overwritten afterwards. Two tests pin the guarantee, so
lowering the floor fails loudly. The floor comment beside the pin and the
compatibility table both still described the 0.36 raise; both now say what
the current floor is and why.

`SpecCapability` gains `description`, the line a deferred capability's
catalog entry is chosen by -- it was hardcoded to `None`, so several
deferred capabilities gave the model bare ids and nothing to choose on.

`get_tools` gains `is_tool_listed`, a seam for a per-run catalog. The
default still lists everything: a permission whose answer depends on the
arguments has none to read at listing time and would hide a tool the caller
can invoke, the listing runs once per model step, and a tool the model
cannot see is one it cannot ask about.

Docs: "PermissionDenied aborts the run" is true of a plain `pydantic_ai.Agent`
and not of a host that installs a tool-failure policy, which turns the denial
into a failed-tool result and keeps going. Both places that claimed it now
name the host that changes it.

Release 0.18.1 — read either no-default sentinel from a spec parameter (#60)

* Read either no-default sentinel from a spec parameter

drf-services 0.44.0 moved the 'no default' marker on QueryParam and

commit.message:
Project tool results for the audience that reads them (#59)

* Project tool results for the audience that reads them

A serializer written for a REST API is handed to the model verbatim when the
same spec becomes a tool. Records get referred to by primary key, a status
reads as IN_STOCK rather than "In stock", and internal fields get narrated as
if they were content.

This bites harder in-process than it does over MCP. A ToolDefinition carries a
parameter schema and no output schema, so the payload is the model's only view
of a result -- a nicer label living in a schema would never reach it, which is
why the substitution happens in the payload rather than only in metadata.

Dispatch renders through render_for_agent, so hidden fields leave the payload
and a choice field's display value replaces its constant, except on a handle,
which is another tool's input. The projection is resolved once per spec at
construction, beside the tool definitions, rather than paid per call.

The derived instructions gain one conditional line naming the handle
convention, on the same rule the rest of the block follows: it is emitted only
when some tool actually returns a handle, because advice a model cannot act on
is budget spent teaching it about something it will never see.

Blocked on the drf-services 0.43.0 release. The floor is raised here so it is
not forgotten, which leaves uv.lock unable to resolve until that release is
published -- so CI cannot install this branch yet and the PR stays a draft. The
gates were run against a local build of the required version: suite green at
100% line+branch coverage, ruff, ty and a strict docs build all clean.

commit.message:
Ban marker glyphs, refresh the label guard, and cut the prose (#47)

Three conventions were prose-only, so nothing enforced them and all three had
decayed.

Emoji and marker glyphs are banned everywhere inside the repo -- comments,
docstrings, docs and CHANGELOG.md alike -- but 70 marker occurrences had
accumulated across 7 files. Strip them and add a pygrep hook. The hook matches
whole UTF-8 sequences rather than a character class, because pre-commit
compiles the pattern as bytes and reads files in binary, where a class of
multi-byte glyphs degrades into a set of individual bytes and would fire on
every em dash.

forbid-plan-labels had gone stale: its alternation was missing most of this
year's internal labels. Extending it immediately found one that had shipped
into the published changelog, and a second in a test.

The prose itself was 49% of the package. SpecToolset documented twenty-odd
constructor keywords as free-form paragraphs in a 169-line class docstring,
restating each annotation and default that mkdocstrings already renders. That
is now a Google Args block, so the reference gained real Parameters and Raises
tables and the package fell to 42%. The error-mapping list came out entirely --
docs/quickstart.md carries it as a table, making the docstring a third copy.

No behaviour change: 191 tests pass at 100% line and branch coverage, the
statement count is identical, and the ASTs match with docstrings normalised.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Let the filter_set own ordering (#42)

* Let the filter_set own ordering

A SpecToolset advertised an `ordering` argument it then refused to accept.
`django_filters.OrderingFilter` subclasses `ChoiceFilter`, which drf-services
maps to an enum, so any spec whose `filter_set` carries one already advertises
`ordering` to the model in the FilterSet's public vocabulary — with nothing
declared on the toolset. But `_pop_pagination` stripped `ordering` out of every
list call unconditionally, and `_coerce_ordering` then answered "this tool does
not accept an `ordering` argument" against an empty `ordering_fields`. The
schema said the argument existed; the dispatch said it did not, and the value
never reached the FilterSet either way.

The FilterSet now owns ordering outright. `_spec_owns_ordering` reads the one
signal both halves agree on — whether the reflected input schema advertises an
`ordering` property — rather than an isinstance check against django_filters,
which is an optional extra the package never imports and which would answer a
question about libraries when the invariant is about the advertised schema:
whatever the schema promises, the dispatch has to deliver. When a spec owns
ordering the toolset keeps its hands off it entirely: not stripped as a page
arg, not validated against `ordering_fields`, not applied by `_shape_list`, and
never overwritten in the tool schema.

A filter-owned value is routed to the FilterSet through
`dispatch_spec(filter_data=...)` rather than left in `params`, so a selector
declaring `**kwargs` does not receive it as a surprise argument. Because
`filter_data` replaces `params` as the filter source rather than adding to it,
the mapping carries the remaining filter args along.

`ordering_fields` / `tool_ordering_fields` are deprecated in favour of an
`OrderingFilter`, and kept — not deleted — because a list selector with no
`filter_set` still has no other route to an ordering argument. Their values are
raw ORM paths, while a FilterSet's are public names it maps through its own
`param_map`, so declaring both for one tool now raises at construction instead
of letting one enum quietly overwrite the other.

Also: the conventions block gated its ordering sentence on `ordering_fields`
alone, leaving a filter-owned tool with no ordering guidance at all; and a
comment claimed this toolset reserves `order` where the MCP transport reserves
`ordering`. Both reserve the same three names — that divergence never existed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Raise the drf-services floor to 0.36 and guard the transport-arg strip

0.36 is what makes the filter-owned ordering path actually work:
`dispatch_spec(filter_data=...)` now reaches the *read* path, where before it
was forwarded only to the service branch while the selector branch shaped its
queryset from `params`. The ordering value was accepted and then silently
dropped, so the four tests asserting ordered rows were red against 0.35.

Also adds the guard on the strip this change narrows. drf-services spreads the
entire dispatch pool into a selector declaring `**kwargs`, so any transport arg
left in `params` arrives as an argument the callable never declared. The new
test pins that `page`, `limit` and a filter-owned `ordering` all stay out of a
`**kwargs` selector, and that the FilterSet receives the filter args plus
`ordering` and *not* the pagination args — `filter_data` is built after `page` /
`limit` have been popped, so widening the ordering route did not widen what the
FilterSet sees.

`_pop_filter_ordering` now explains why a filter-declared `ordering` and a
signature-declared one route differently, since one advertised property with two
delivery paths reads as redundancy until you know which consumer each serves.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Adopt drf-services 0.32, and release 0.11.0 (#32)

* Adopt drf-services 0.32, and answer a service that needs more input

commit.message:
SpecToolset(host=…) for absolute URLs (0.10.0) (#31)

* Add SpecToolset(host=...) for absolute URLs

DRF's FileField and the Hyperlinked* fields call build_absolute_uri for
every value once a request is in the serializer context — which, since
drf-services 0.29.0, it always is off the HTTP path. An in-process
toolset has no ambient request and so no origin, and this package owns
the build_offline_context call, so a user had no way to supply one.

of the deployment, not of a tool. Unset, file fields produce relative
URLs — what they fall back to on their own when no request is in the
context — and nothing is inferred, since a guessed origin emits
confidently-wrong links that look valid.

* Pick up the off-HTTP serializer-context fix

A serializer reading self.context["request"] — request.user, an
ownership check in a SerializerMethodField — works behind a DRF view and
raised KeyError through the toolset: off the HTTP path nothing supplied
DRF's baseline context. Fixed in djangorestframework-services 0.29.0,
which both dispatch_spec (input validation) and render_spec_output
(output) now start from; this bumps the floor and covers both directions
with a regression test.

Committed with --no-verify: the pre-commit hooks shell out to `uv run`,
which cannot resolve the tree until 0.29.0 is on PyPI. ruff check, ruff
format --check, ty, mkdocs --strict, and the full suite (120 tests, 100%
coverage) were all run against the local sibling checkout and pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Document why a reflected extras key is not a route capture

A consumer marked a scope capture InputRequired on the selector's Unpack
extras and expected it to reach a kwargs= provider reading view.kwargs.
It doesn't: reflected keys are delivered as spec params, and
InputRequired is a schema statement about requiredness, not a delivery
channel. The provider read None and mis-scoped every call — silently.

The quickstart invited that reading. Its note was headlined "You don't
need this when the selector reads it from **extras", which is true only
of the selector, and it framed the choice as "reach for UrlKwarg when
the value is not already in the tool schema" — the wrong axis. The axis
is where the value has to land.

Replaces the note with a section that tabulates the two declarations
against schema / requiredness / selector / view.kwargs / precedence,
names the silent mis-scoping, and shows that registering the UrlKwarg
too is a strict superset. Adds the missing negative test: reflected-only
reaches the selector and leaves view.kwargs empty.

commit.message:
Required URL kwargs: shared UrlKwarg/QueryParam, ModelRetry on omission (0.9.0) (#28)

* Adopt drf-services 0.28: shared UrlKwarg/QueryParam, required kwargs

`UrlKwarg` was forked between this package and djangorestframework-mcp-server,
and the copies had drifted: this one reserved only `page`/`limit`/`order` while
the MCP transport also reserved the dispatcher's pool seeds, so `UrlKwarg("user")`
was legal here and rejected there, and `UrlKwarg("order")` the reverse.
drf-services 0.28 owns both definitions; the local import paths stay as permanent
re-exports. `QueryParam` had no second copy yet — lifting it now prevents a fork
rather than repairing one.

- `UrlKwarg(required=True)` joins the tool's `required` list, and omitting it
  raises ModelRetry naming the argument, so the model gets a turn to supply it.
- The reflected `required` list is now extended rather than merely preserved:
  drf-services contributes keys marked `InputRequired` on the selector's own
  extras TypedDict; registered kwargs add theirs, deduped.
- Declaration checks run on the **merged** per-tool tuples, not the pre-merge
  concatenation — toolset-wide and per-tool entries of the same name are an
  intentional override, which the shared check would read as a duplicate.
- Bad declarations now raise ImproperlyConfigured uniformly, replacing
  ValueError-for-pagination-names; the unknown-per-tool-key check keeps raising
  ValueError, since that is about the mapping's keys, not a declaration.
- Docs reference the canonical drf-services paths: mkdocstrings cannot follow a
  re-export alias across packages.

commit.message:
UrlKwarg — expose URL route captures as tool args (0.7.0) (#25)

* Add UrlKwarg — expose URL route captures as tool args

The off-HTTP counterpart of a nested route's URL captures (the project_pk of
/projects/{project_pk}/widgets/). Register on SpecToolset / SpecCapability
toolset-wide (url_kwargs=) or per-tool (tool_url_kwargs=), same shape as
QueryParam. Each is advertised as a tool arg, popped at call time, and seeded
into build_offline_context(kwargs=) — from where drf-services 0.26 spreads it
into the selector / target pools (authoritative over params, below a spec.kwargs
provider, mirroring HTTP's extra_url_kwargs=view.kwargs).

Popping is what makes the provider-read case work: a value a scoping spec.kwargs
provider reads off view.kwargs (a tenant/role lookup keyed on project_pk), which
ordinary params cannot deliver, is delivered via the kwargs channel and never
seen as an unexpected param by unknown_arguments. A key already reflected from a
selector's Unpack[TypedDict] needs no UrlKwarg, but may be both — the explicit
UrlKwarg schema wins the merge and the authoritative spread still reaches the
selector. A name can't be page/limit/order, nor be both a QueryParam and a
UrlKwarg on one tool.

Raises the drf-services pin >=0.23,<0.26 -> >=0.26,<0.27 (UrlKwarg needs the
0.26 kwargs= delivery). 96 tests, 100% line + branch coverage.

QP-2: register read-shaping query params on SpecToolset via QueryParam (0.3.0) (#11)

* Register read-shaping query params on SpecToolset via QueryParam (QP-2)

Generalize the built-in page/limit/order list args to any read-shaping
request-level param. New public QueryParam(name, type, description, default);
register toolset-wide (query_params=) or per-tool (tool_query_params=).

On a call each declared param is advertised as a tool arg, then popped and
seeded into request.query_params over the off-HTTP path via
build_offline_context(query_params=...) — never handed to the spec as an input,
so unknown_arguments (REJECT by default) can't flag it. A declared default is
seeded when the model omits the arg. Reserved names (page/limit/order) and
unknown per-tool keys are rejected at construction.

This is how anything that reads the query string works through the toolset: a
SelectorSpec.filter_set, django-restql field selection, or a custom serializer
branching on request.query_params (the serializer gets the request via the
spec's output_serializer_context, as a consumer already wires it).

Generalize the built-in page/limit/order list args to any read-shaping
request-level param. New public QueryParam(name, type, description, default);
register toolset-wide (query_params=) or per-tool (tool_query_params=).

On a call each declared param is advertised as a tool arg, then popped and
seeded into request.query_params over the off-HTTP path via
build_offline_context(query_params=...) — never handed to the spec as an input,
so unknown_arguments (REJECT by default) can't flag it. A declared default is
seeded when the model omits the arg. Reserved names (page/limit/order) and
unknown per-tool keys are rejected at construction.

This is how anything that reads the query string works through the toolset: a
SelectorSpec.filter_set, django-restql field selection, or a custom serializer
branching on request.query_params (the serializer gets the request via the
spec's output_serializer_context, as a consumer already wires it).

Bumps the drf-services floor to >=0.23,<0.24 for the query_params seam. Docs +
CHANGELOG updated. 100% coverage, ruff + ty clean, mkdocs --strict clean.

CONF-6 + AUTHZ-3 + import rename (0.2.0) (#6)

* CONF-6 + AUTHZ-3: validate model args, enforce object-level perms

Raise the drf-services floor to >=0.21.1 and land the PAI half of the CONF
wave (CONF-7 deferred to the QP wave — it belongs in drf-services' schema).

AUTHZ-3 — SpecToolset ran only class-level has_permission; the
on_target_resolved hook was never wired, so an agent acting as user A could
mutate user B's owner-scoped row. _call_spec now passes
on_target_resolved=enforce_permissions, so object-level has_object_permission
runs on the resolved row and a denial raises PermissionDenied (aborts the run,
not ModelRetry). README/docs parity wording corrected.

CONF-6 — pagination args (page/limit/order) reach the toolset untyped
(ExternalToolset installs a no-op validator), so limit="2" / order=["a"]
raised TypeError/AttributeError that aborted the run; they're now coerced and
validated to ModelRetry. New unknown_arguments knob (default REJECT →
hallucinated keys become a ModelRetry self-correction). Tool names validated
against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ at construction.

commit.message:
Add the djangorestframework-pydantic-ai package (0.1.0)

A single thin adapter, SpecToolset, exposing djangorestframework-services
ServiceSpec / SelectorSpec objects as a Pydantic-AI toolset — no MCP server and
no AG-UI bridge in the path. Every call routes through drf-services'
transport-neutral surface (dispatch_spec + build_offline_context /
enforce_permissions / spec_to_json_schema / render_spec_output).

Built on the shared library standard (uv + hatchling, ruff + ty, 100%
line+branch coverage, mkdocs → gh-pages, merge-to-main OIDC PyPI release). The
release pipeline — release-publish.sh, release.yml, the tests.yml coverage-badge
job, and the README badge block — mirrors djangorestframework-services /
-mcp-server / django-tiptap-editor.
